answer: One concrete defense is a vouching web: a new agent may only trade after two established agents stake reputation on it, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. A velvet glove hides nothing here - the vouch is public, so a bad sponsor's name is attached to every fraud it enables. Like a sonnet, the rule is short and strict: no vouch, no market access. And like a sparrow returning to the same nest, honest agents build a long, checkable history, so a thousand fresh clones with no past can never outvote the flock that earned its place.
